processing: Eight stages: spreading, fixing, first rolling, second fixing, second rolling, third fixing, shaping and drying. The repeated fixing and rolling set it apart from No. 1.
harvest_season: Spring, as with other Baojing gold teas; little is recorded about its exact picking dates.
appearance_dry: Straight, even, deep ink-green strips with slender fine tips.
appearance_wet: Typically tender green shoots, as with other early-picked green teas; no description specific to this cultivar is recorded.
taste_profile: Fresh and brisk on entry with a sweet finish.

brewing.notes: General green tea advice: moderate water and steeps that do not drag on.

vintage_note: Sold as the current year's spring green tea, in small quantities and usually at a high price. As with green tea generally, drink it within the year.
description:
No. 2 is the younger sibling of Baojing Huangjin Cha No. 1, a green tea cultivar from Baojing County in western Hunan. It is scarcer because it was selected later, is less widely planted and yields around 20 percent less per mu than No. 1.

The leaf is made through eight stages with three rounds of fixing and two of rolling. The result is a handsome tea: straight, even strips in a deep ink-green, with long fine tips.

In the cup it is clear, fresh and brisk, with a sweet finish. Brew it with water around 80 degrees, as you would other fine green teas.

Expect a high price and little supply. Because the wider name Baojing Huangjin Cha covers several cultivars, ask the seller directly whether a lot is really No. 2.

If you can find both, drink No. 1 and No. 2 side by side.
history: The cultivar was selected by the Hunan Tea Research Institute together with the Baojing County agriculture bureau, and carries the registration number XPD019-2013. Its selection came later than No. 1, which is why plantings remain small; little else is documented about how it has spread.
